findings.name: Introduction states the price-access gain at any fixed strength; Prop. A.9 holds only at r_1
findings.problem: The introduction says that at fixed incumbent strength, access to prices raises expected target proceeds and net acquisition surplus. Proposition A.9 and Sec. 6.1 fix r=r_1 under the conditions of Proposition 2. At r_0 there is no trade and the price carries no information, so access changes nothing. Table 2 shows the price-hidden row at r=1.2 equal to the equilibrium row. Read as a general claim, the introduction contradicts the formal result and the table.

findings.reasoning: Verified. main.tex:233-235 says "At fixed incumbent strength, access to prices raises expected target proceeds and acquisition surplus net of preparation costs". Proposition A.9 (main.tex:2349-2357) holds only at r=r_1 under the conditions of Proposition 2, and Sec. 6.1 (main.tex:1061) likewise says "Hold the incumbent at r_1". Table 2 (tables/table2_equilibrium_controls.tex) gives identical "Price hidden, r=1.2" and "Weak incumbent (r=1.2)" rows (E=0.250000, O_H=0.125000, R_T=0.392708), so the gain is zero at r_0. This is a qualifier dropped in a restatement, which the rubric grades Mid, and it matches F15 (Mid) and paper-sync row 10. The introduction never names r_1: it says "the strong incumbent" (main.tex:208-213), so the fix should use those words. Main.tex:1060 ("at a fixed level of competition") is qualified in the very next sentence and needs no change.

Sec. 4.3 promises that 'Appendix A reports the certificate margins', but no enclosure or value of k - rho Delta_T(r_j)/2 appears in Appendix A, the OA or the registry. Only the Psi endpoint signs and the Gamma_H lower bounds are reported.
findings.evidence: main.tex:870 "Appendix A reports the certificate margins"; main.tex:1944-1946 "No trade is also an equilibrium at each certified strength because \(\rho\Delta_T(r_j)/2\le k\) there ... the pooling margin is enclosed with the same outward arithmetic." grep 'pooling margin' finds 2 hits (both main.tex:1945-1949) and none in online_appendix.tex, quantity_registry.csv or quantity_manifest.csv.
findings.proposed_fix: Report the three enclosed pooling margins beside (A.19), or replace the sentence with the analytical argument r_j < r_N = 1.747877538 (Prop. A.4) and drop 'enclosed'.

findings.name: Log-odds written as log(tau/(1-tau)) and as undefined 'logit'; 'logistic' also used as a function
findings.problem: Eq. (12) defines x* = (b/2)log(tau/(1-tau)). Appendix A.3 then writes the same threshold with \operatorname{logit}(\tau), which the paper never defines. Lemma OA.2 uses 'logistic(.)' as the inverse function, although 'logistic' otherwise names the noise law. The subscript 'log' on x^*_{log} (main.tex:1991) means logistic, not logarithm.
findings.evidence: main.tex:766 "x^*&=\frac b2\log\frac\tau{1-\tau}"; main.tex:1820 "x^*(r,v)&=\frac{b\operatorname{logit}(\tau)+1-v}{2}". Counts: 'logit' main 1, OA 6; '\log\frac' log-odds form main 2 (766, 1975), OA 1 (725). online_appendix.tex:817 "\mu_-=\operatorname{logistic}(\operatorname{logit}\pi-2/b)"
findings.proposed_fix: Define logit(u) = log(u/(1-u)) once at eq. (12) and use it everywhere, or keep the log-ratio form throughout. Write the inverse as \Lambda(\cdot) or spell out (1+e^{-y})^{-1}.

findings.proposed_fix: Render the node label as "exact event: floor equality \(p_L\)" and "exact event: ceiling equality \(p_H\)".

findings.name: Mixed-strategy integrals written as d\sigma_H(q) in the paper and \sigma_\theta(dq) in the OA
findings.problem: The same flow density a_theta(x) is written with two measure-integration conventions, and the OA mixes both (\sigma_\theta(dq) in A.1, d\sigma_\pm(q) in A.7).
findings.evidence: main.tex:596 "a_H(x)&=\int f(x-q)\,d\sigma_H(q)"; online_appendix.tex:256 "a_\theta(x)&=\int_{[-1,1]}f(x-q)\,\sigma_\theta(dq)"; online_appendix.tex:291 "\(\sigma_H(dq)\sigma_L(dq')\)"; online_appendix.tex:879 "\(a_+(x)=\int f(x-q)d\sigma_+(q)\)". Counts: 'd\sigma' main 5, OA 3; '(dq)' forms OA 2.
findings.proposed_fix: Use \int f(x-q)\,\sigma_\theta(dq) (or d\sigma_\theta(q)) in both documents.

findings.name: OA result numbering shares one counter across lemmas and propositions, and the lemmas have no titles
findings.problem: The OA's only formal results are Lemma OA.1, Lemma OA.2 and Proposition OA.3. A reader of 'Proposition OA.3' will look for Propositions OA.1 and OA.2, which do not exist. Every paper result header has the form '(title; status)', but the two lemmas carry only '(analytical)'.
findings.evidence: online_appendix.tex:800 "\textbf{Lemma OA.1 (analytical).}"; online_appendix.tex:815 "\textbf{Lemma OA.2 (analytical).}"; online_appendix.tex:1548 "Proposition OA.3 ... (price pooling at fixed orders; analytical)". grep 'Proposition OA.[12]' finds 0 hits.
findings.proposed_fix: Number propositions and lemmas separately, or drop Prop. OA.3 in favour of Prop. A.10 (see M47). Give the lemmas short titles, e.g. '(convex trading costs; analytical)' and '(unequal priors; analytical)'.
